summary_short: e.l.f. Beauty's fiscal Q4 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) revenue was $449M, up 35.1% y/y but down 8.2% q/q, while the quarter swung to a $49M net loss (diluted EPS -$0.82) after three straight profitable quarters this fiscal year.
summary_long: This 10-K covers e.l.f. Beauty's fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (fiscal Q4); the filing doesn't isolate standalone-quarter causes. Full-year net sales rose 25% to $1.64B — rhode (acquired August 2025) added $293.5M, pricing/mix added $333.5M, partly offset by $10.5M lower volume. Gross margin fell ~50bp to 70.7% on tariffs. SG&A rose 32% on marketing, compensation and D&A; a $57.6M rhode earnout fair-value charge and interest expense nearly tripling to $35.3M on new acquisition debt cut full-year operating income to $73.6M from $158.0M and net income to $26.3M from $112.1M. Cash rose to $289.7M on $600M new term debt and $50M revolver draws; no share buybacks this quarter. No forward guidance given.

drivers.explanation: Not explained in the release -- the 10-K reports Q4 net sales, gross profit, net income and EPS in its quarterly-summary note but does not analyze why this standalone quarter swung to a loss; only full fiscal-year causes are discussed in the MD&A.

FY2026 net sales +25% to $1.64B: the rhode Acquisition (closed Aug 2025) added $293.5M, existing business added $29.5M; higher average item price/mix added $333.5M, partly offset by $10.5M lower volume.
FY2026 gross margin was 70.7%, down ~50bp y/y, driven primarily by tariffs and partly offset by pricing; this is a full fiscal-year figure -- the 10-K doesn't isolate this quarter.

FY2026 SG&A rose 32% ($248.4M) on marketing/distribution (+$129.1M), compensation (+$55.1M) and D&A (+$35.0M); the company also booked a $57.6M contingent-consideration fair-value charge tied to rhode's earnout outperformance.
FY2026 interest expense nearly tripled to $35.3M after the Fifth Amendment's $600M Term Facility funded the rhode Acquisition, and the effective tax rate rose to 35% from 23%.

Cash rose to $289.7M mainly on $600.0M of new term-loan proceeds and $50.0M of revolver draws used to fund the rhode Acquisition; the company states it repurchased no shares in the quarter ended March 31, 2026.
